bull.b: Early clinical efficacy and favorable tolerability provide a stronger basis for advancing OPGx-BEST1 than an unvalidated program. If these results are reproduced in larger cohorts, they could support regulatory progress and improve the company’s strategic position in inherited retinal disease gene therapy.

FDA alignment on a potential pivotal endpoint and Phase 3 requirements reduces regulatory uncertainty around the lead program. A defined route toward 2027 dosing can focus development resources, create clearer milestones, and improve the program’s prospects of reaching a registrational trial.

A larger estimated patient population and an over-enrolled higher-dose cohort expand the potential commercial relevance of OPGx-BEST1 while generating broader clinical evidence. Keeping Phase 3 and manufacturing timelines on track could support scalable development if efficacy and safety hold.

bear.b: The very large TTM operating and net losses show that current revenue is not covering the company’s development cost base. Persistently negative profitability reduces internal funding capacity and makes future progress dependent on successfully financing continued clinical work.

Operating and free cash flow were both about -$53.4M TTM, worsening from roughly -$35.3M in 2025 and remaining negative since 2023. This sustained burn can consume liquidity and require repeated external funding before products generate meaningful cash.

Negative equity alongside $34.9M of debt marks a material deterioration from the debt-free, positive-equity position reported in 2023–2025. This weaker capitalization limits financial flexibility and can make raising funds for clinical development more difficult.
